long_biography.plain_text:
Australian businessman Kerry Stokes’s purchase of the Rothschild Prayer Book prompted him to collect more medieval and Renaissance art. He assembled stained glass, sculpture and paintings around the illuminated manuscript. These works became the basis of an exhibition at Melbourne’s Ian Potter Museum of Art, where visitors could see the book alongside objects from its period.

As a television proprietor, Stokes put straightforward dealing at the centre of his business philosophy. He favoured frank conversations when delivering difficult news and believed a company’s first obligation was to its customers. He attributed his respect for working people to having experienced hardship himself.

confidence.reason: The exhibiting university museum directly describes the manuscript-led acquisition programme and exhibition. His recorded ABC interview directly supports the business philosophy and self-attributed effect of hardship. No psychology beyond those statements is inferred.
